title: Andhra and Odisha Activate Disaster Machinery Ahead of October 28 Cyclone Landfall
excerpt: With a very severe cyclonic storm forecast to cross between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28, Odisha deployed 60 ODRAF units and 17 NDRF teams under a zero-casualty target and Andhra activated control rooms across 12 coastal districts.
body:
• Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have moved to full cyclone preparations, with landfall expected on the forenoon to afternoon of October 28 between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam and the adjoining south Odisha coast.
  • The IMD forecasts the Bay of Bengal system to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by October 27, with sustained winds of 115-125 kmph and gusts to 140 kmph.
  • Odisha has issued a red warning for Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri, deployed 60 ODRAF units and 17 NDRF teams, and set a zero-casualty target; Andhra has activated control rooms across 12 coastal districts.
  • Fishermen have been told not to venture to sea until October 29 and vessels at sea to return immediately; residents in low-lying coastal areas should follow district evacuation orders and IMD bulletins.

Andhra Pradesh and Odisha activated their disaster machinery on Sunday as a Bay of Bengal depression was forecast to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the coast on October 28, prompting red warnings, rescue deployments and orders for fishermen to stay ashore until October 29.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh by the forenoon of October 28, according to Mirror Now. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, after a review meeting, placed the crossing in the afternoon of October 28 somewhere between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, with the greatest impact expected between Kakinada and Gopalpur. This update follows our earlier report on the storm's formation, Bay of Bengal Storm, Likely Named Arnab, to Hit Odisha-Andhra Coast on October 28.

What is new: preparations, not just formation

The change since the formation story is the scale of preparation now under way. In Odisha, the government has cancelled leave, assigned specific responsibilities to departments, and deployed 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) units and 17 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams, with fire services on high alert. A red warning is in place for Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri, where rainfall could exceed 20 cm in 24 hours, according to the IMD reporting in Mirror Now and The Times of Bengal.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2114279178539516039

"As always, our primary objective remains the same: zero casualties."

— Mohan Charan Majhi, Odisha Chief Minister

In Andhra Pradesh, control rooms have been activated to monitor more than 30,000 fishing boats across 12 coastal districts. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast for coastal districts, Yanam and Rayalaseema between October 26 and 29, with thunderstorms and lightning. Schools have been shut in affected Odisha districts as a precaution, and government holidays have been cancelled in vulnerable areas.

Forecast track and intensity

The system began as a well-marked low-pressure area over the central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal. The IMD expects it to become a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26 and to keep intensifying as it moves west-northwest towards the Andhra coast, according to Fact. If it reaches cyclonic-storm strength it will be named Arnab, a name contributed by Bangladesh to the regional naming list.

By October 27 the storm is forecast to reach very severe cyclonic storm strength, with maximum sustained winds of 115-125 kmph and gusts to 140 kmph at landfall. The IMD has issued a pre-cyclone watch for Andhra Pradesh and the adjoining south Odisha coast, and heavy to extremely heavy rain is expected over coastal Andhra and Odisha from October 27 to 29.

What residents should do now

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea until October 29, and all vessels already at sea have been directed to return to the coast immediately. People in low-lying areas along the Bapatla to Vizianagaram stretch and in Odisha's red-warning districts should be ready to move to cyclone shelters when district authorities issue evacuation orders, and should follow IMD bulletins and local control-room announcements rather than waiting for landfall day. The wider system is also expected to bring heavy rain to parts of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar and Chhattisgarh in late October.

For diaspora readers with family on the coast, the actionable window is the next 48 hours: confirm family members know their nearest cyclone shelter, keep phones charged ahead of possible power cuts on October 28-29, and check travel plans to Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Bhubaneswar against airline and rail advisories as the landfall window nears.

What happens next

Forecasters will narrow the landfall point as the storm intensifies on October 26-27. State governments are expected to begin evacuations from the most exposed low-lying villages ahead of the October 28 crossing, and the IMD will issue updated warnings on wind, rainfall and storm surge. The exact track and peak intensity remain subject to change, and officials in both states say preparedness, not prediction, is the priority until the system makes landfall.
